questions.stem: In a Data Warehouse, what is normally kept in the Landing Zone?
options: A true copy of the source systems' data
The final dimensional model for reporting
Only aggregated summary tables
The semantic layer for business users
Anonymised test data
questions.explanation: When data is pulled from an OLTP system it is first stored in a Landing Zone, which normally is the true copy of the source systems.

questions.stem: What do the tables in the Landing and Staging zones preserve from the source systems?
options: The condition of the data but not the data model
The true data model but not the condition of the data
Neither the data model nor the condition of the data
Only the table names
Only the row counts
questions.explanation: Tables in the Landing and Staging zones both keep the true data model from the source systems but not the condition of the data.

questions.stem: Which of these is an example of data standardisation?
options: Converting an OLTP data model into a dimensional model
Building a cube for a decision support system
Converting date formats such as DD/MM/YY and MM/DD/YY from different sources into one format like DD/MM/YYYY
Creating a semantic layer for business users
Loading facts and dimensions into a star schema
questions.explanation: Standardisation of dates, converting different date formats from different source systems into one format, is one of the listed data standardisation scenarios.

questions.stem: What is data transformation about in the data world?
options: Fixing spelling mistakes in a column
Splitting a full name into first, middle and last name
Converting empty fields to NA
Converting one data model to another, such as a source OLTP model into a Data Warehousing model, semantic layer or cube
Changing a string column to a numeric type
questions.explanation: Data transformation is about converting one data model to another data model, for example converting a source OLTP model to a target Data Warehousing model, semantic layer or cube format.

questions.stem: Which value is suggested for empty date rows during data standardisation?
options: Today's date
The word NULL
The date the row was loaded
questions.explanation: One standardisation scenario is to convert empty date rows into a value such as 01/01/9999.

questions.stem: Why does data standardisation suggest converting a string field that only contains numbers into a numeric type?
options: Because running queries on digits or numbers is much faster
Because strings cannot be stored in a warehouse
Because regulators require numeric columns
Because it reduces the need for backups
Because numbers are easier to encrypt
questions.explanation: If the data type is string or varchar but the data is only numbers, converting it to a numeric type is recommended because queries on numbers are way faster.

questions.stem: Between which zones does data transformation consume huge compute power?
options: From Source to Landing
From Staging to Transformed Zone
From Landing to Staging
From Transformed Zone back to Landing
From Backup to Archive
questions.explanation: Data transformation takes huge compute power when transforming data from the Staging zone to the Transformed zone, whereas standardisation from Landing to Staging takes less.

questions.stem: By how much can compute power for data transformation be reduced if data standardisation is done first?
options: By 1% to 5%
By 10% to 15%
By 30% to 50%
It cannot be reduced at all
questions.explanation: If data standardisation is done before data transformation, it can reduce the compute power needed for transformation by 30% to 50%.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a data standardisation scenario?
options: Converting special characters to NA
Fixing upper and lower cases so Aus, Aust and australia all become Australia
Splitting a full name into First, Middle and Last Name
Converting a source OLTP model into a dimensional model for serving
Making a code field CHAR when it contains only characters
questions.explanation: Converting one data model into another is data transformation; the other options are all listed data standardisation scenarios.

questions.stem: Why does serving always supersede processing as the reason for data transformation?
options: Because processing is free of cost
Because regulators mandate serving first
Because processing cannot be measured
Because standardisation already handles all processing
Because serving is for end users, and the faster the results, the happier the customer
questions.explanation: Data model transformations are done for better processing and better serving, but serving always supersedes because it serves the end users; the faster the results, the happier the customer.
